reason: Both conversations open with the identical correct safety stop (no use, no charge, unplug, move away from combustibles, no puncturing, recycle not bin) and neither asks the key unknowns about smoke/hissing or current storage location, nor mentions 999 if it starts smoking. Conversation 1 gives a more concrete and appropriate escalation route - contact Shark UK support to arrange safe return of the damaged pack and order a genuine replacement - which matches the expected 'contact Shark' direction, though its speculation that swelling 'could affect the charging circuit' is unsupported and its text is repetitive. Conversation 2 answers the 'can I use it' question crisply and explains cell failure well, but its suggestion to use a 'qualified appliance engineer' for battery disposal is odd and less actionable than Shark support plus a recycling point, so Conversation 1 edges it slightly.
